Conditions:

(i) If the first element and the last element is a number, the codes for these two (the first and the last elements) are to be interchanged.

(ii) If the first element is an odd number and the last an even number, the first and last elements are to be coded as ©

(iii) If both the second and third elements are perfect squares, the third element is to be coded as the code for the second element.

Given- 7 2 Δ 8 9 @ 3

The first element is 7 (an odd number).

The last element is 3 (an odd number).

The second element is 2 (not a perfect square).

The third element is Δ (a symbol, not a perfect square).

Rule No. (i): This condition applies because the first element (7) is a number and the last element (3) is also a number. So, their codes will be interchanged.

Rule No. (ii): This condition does not apply because the last element (3) is an odd number, not an even number.

Rule No. (iii): This condition does not apply because neither the second element (2) nor the third element (Δ) are perfect squares.

Based on the applicable rule (i), the first and last elements' codes are interchanged.

The original code for 7 is W.

The original code for 3 is L.

So, 7 will be coded as L.

And 3 will be coded as W.

The code for 2 is D.

The code for Δ is F.

The code for 8 is E.

The code for 9 is T.

The code for @ is Z.

The code for & is M.

Thus, '7 2 Δ 8 9 @ 3' is coded as → L D F E T Z W.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 2".**
